interactiveCells.question: What was the original clinical disease target of mRNA platform technology prior to COVID-19?
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer: Therapeutic oncology vaccines targeting patient-specific tumour neoantigens (e.g., metastatic melanoma, colorectal cancers).

interactiveCells.question: How did the trial trajectory of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines differ from conventional drug development?
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer: Accelerated overlapping clinical trial phases (Phase I/II/III run concurrently) under pandemic public health emergency authorisations.

interactiveCells.question: What is the distinction between a 'surrogate endpoint' and a 'clinical primary endpoint'?
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer: Surrogate endpoints are measurable biomarkers (e.g. antibody titres or T-cell counts); clinical primary endpoints measure direct patient health outcomes (e.g. disease prevention, overall survival).

interactiveCells.question: Why are surrogate endpoints (like CD8+ T-cell expansion) heavily relied upon in early-phase oncology trials?
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer: Tumour regression and progression-free survival require years to evaluate, so immune activation biomarkers provide immediate proof-of-mechanism.

interactiveCells.question: What are the core sections required in the Mock NEA drafted in this lesson?
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer: Literature Review (mechanism and justification) and Methodology Evaluation (trial design critique and endpoint comparison).

interactiveCells.question: State two mandatory criteria for embedding citations into the Mock NEA draft.
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer: Include at least two peer-reviewed sources, cited using author-date Harvard in-text format and matched to a complete reference list.
